subject: Re: HealthSafe request - no-adaptive-learning confirmation and subprocessor inventory
messages:
From: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@healthsafe.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSafe Legal <legal@healthsafe.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: No-adaptive-training confirmation + subprocessor inventory

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security and legal teams are reviewing Redwood for an enterprise pilot. As part of our DPA diligence we need two things confirmed in writing before we proceed:

1) A written confirmation that interactions sent to Redwood for our tenant will not be used to adapt or retrain any public models (no-adaptive-training / no-learning). We understand operational telemetry for service health is different — please explicitly state what is or is not considered "model improvement" data.

2) A current inventory of subprocessors with region of processing, plus any planned changes over the next 90 days. If you have onshore KMS or EU-only processing options, please indicate how we can opt our tenant to those lanes.

Attached is our short questionnaire (PDF) — can you provide answers and any supporting operational evidence (audit logs, KMS residency screenshots, export paths) by EOD Friday?

Also, we will need an initial redline of the no-train language that Redwood is willing to commit to for a pilot (we are not asking for irrevocable legal language yet, but must show our risk committee a concrete statement).

Appreciate your help — looping in legal.

Best,
Emma Taylor
Head of Platform Security
HealthSafe

Attachment: HealthSafe_DPA_no-train_questionnaire.pdf (1 page PDF)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@healthsafe.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: No-adaptive-training confirmation + subprocessor inventory

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the questionnaire. High-level answers below; we'll follow up with the evidence pack and a proposed contract excerpt.

Summary (high level)
- No-adaptive-training: For our Hosted API offering used in your trial, Redwood will not use customer inputs or outputs to update public models or include them in any model training corpus. We separate telemetry (health/metrics/aggregates) from model training pipelines; only explicitly opt-in labeled datasets enter any training process.

- Subprocessors & KMS: Attached is our current subprocessor inventory (CSV). We support an EU-only processing lane for enterprise customers with contract-level residency controls and an onshore KMS option (bring-your-own KMS or Redwood-managed EU KMS).

What we'll provide by Friday:
- Evidence pack: audit log extracts showing tenant-level access controls, example KMS key policy, and a short runbook describing how we isolate tenant data from training pipelines.
- Proposed redline: a draft DPA snippet that commits to the pilot-scoped no-adaptive-training guarantee and the operational exclusions (telemetry, ephemeral caching) you mentioned.

A couple of clarifying Qs so we scope the evidence correctly:
1) Do you need full historical audit logs or a 30-day sample?
2) For the KMS option, do you prefer Redwood-managed EU keys or will HealthSafe bring its own keys (we can support either)?

I'll loop in Kimberly for contract language and Dev for the ops artifacts.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_proposed_subprocessors.csv (CSV - 3 rows)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@healthsafe.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSafe Legal <legal@healthsafe.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: No-adaptive-training confirmation + subprocessor inventory

Hi Emma / David —

Thanks, David — this matches what we discussed internally. Emma — attaching a short redline excerpt (PDF) that we would be comfortable agreeing to for a pilot: it commits to a limited-scope "no-adaptive-training" for customer interactions and defines operational exceptions (service telemetry and aggregated metrics that do not include customer prompts/responses). The PDF also lists our standard subprocessors and residency lanes.

From the legal side, a couple of notes for HealthSafe to consider:
- Pilot scope vs. enterprise SLA: We can commit to the no-adaptive-training promise for the pilot term (90 days) with documented controls; an enterprise, longer-term commitment requires an amendment and proof obligations (evidence cadence).
- Escrow / exportability: If HealthSafe requires output-escrow or daily exports of tenant prompts, we can add an export SLA and provide SFTP or API export options.
- KMS specifics: If you bring your own keys (BYOK) we will not have decryption access and can commit to key residency controls in the DPA.

Please review the attached redline (dpa_excerpt_redline.pdf) and the DocuSign link below for a quick pilot amendment signature path if you want to accelerate.

DocuSign (pilot amendment): https://app.docusign.com/documents/XYZ-HealthSafe-HS-2941

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_excerpt_redline.pdf

4) Ops: Confirm subprocessors CSV is up-to-date and add an ETA for any planned changes in the next 90 days.

Target: have the evidence pack uploaded to the secure Drive folder and a short summary email back to Emma by EOD Thursday (2026-06-18). If any of you see blockers (BYOK, escrow path), flag now.

Thanks — I'll own the reply to Emma once we have the pack.

-David
